page: Microsoft Azure E8ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by a 64-bit ARM architecture featuring Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores mapped to 8 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, avoiding virtualization overhead from simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a large 128 MB L3 cache array. With 64.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It includes no bundled local ephemeral storage, directing storage I/O toward network-attached Premium Storage disks, and features zero dedicated hardware accelerators.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate distinct strengths in the memory subsystem. PassMark memory testing places the E8ps_v6 in the top 10 percent of recorded results, underpinned by uncached memory read bandwidth of 164.94 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 71.92 GB/sec. Compression efficiency is also notable, with single-threaded gzip throughput ranking in the upper 25 percent. Conversely, CPU-bound tests remain within the median range, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 9365 and PassMark CPU score of 7770.77. Weaknesses emerge in cryptographic operations and AI token processing, where PassMark encryption and medium model prompt processing test within the lower performance quartiles due to instruction set constraints.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the instance emphasizes high memory density per core, maximizing capacity for memory-resident datasets without paying the operational premium of x86-based equivalents. The lack of local storage requires users to account for network disk performance and overhead. The hardware profile is best matched to memory-bound enterprise applications, including Redis key-value caching, relational and operational databases, distributed analytics pipelines, and general memory-intensive web serving infrastructure.
description: Microsoft Azure E8ps_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by an 8-core Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated physical cores with single-threading, alongside 128 MB of L3 cache. The instance features 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 gigabyte-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive architectures. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached premium storage for persistence, and no integrated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for PassMark memory bandwidth, supported by strong gzip compression capabilities. While general multi-core compute and compilation speeds fall squarely in the mid-range spectrum, cryptographic and LLM prompt processing exhibit performance penalties compared to x86 platforms. The configuration offers cost efficiency for memory footprint capacity rather than compute-heavy acceleration, making it an effective choice for in-memory databases, Redis caches, and data analytics.
